definitions.explanation: The main gate or entrance to a school campus. A prominent feature of Japanese schools, often the site of morning greetings by teachers and the backdrop for graduation photos.

examples.japanese: {校門|こうもん}の{前|まえ}で{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: We arranged to meet in front of the school gate.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}、{校門|こうもん}で{先生|せんせい}が{挨拶|あいさつ}をしていた。
examples.english: In the morning, a teacher was greeting students at the school gate.

examples.japanese: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}の{日|ひ}、{校門|こうもん}の{前|まえ}で{友達|ともだち}と{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}った。
examples.english: On graduation day, I took photos with friends in front of the school gate.

notes:
{校門|こうもん} is the main gate or entrance to a school campus. It holds both practical and symbolic significance in Japanese school culture.

ETYMOLOGY:
{校|こう} (school) + {門|もん} (gate).

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {校門|こうもん} serves as a symbolic boundary between the school and the outside world. Common scenes at the gate:
- Teachers standing at the gate in the morning to greet students ({朝|あさ}の{挨拶|あいさつ})
- Uniform and appearance checks at strict schools
- Graduation photos taken in front of the gate

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {校門|こうもん}の{前|まえ}で: in front of the school gate
- {校門|こうもん}をくぐる: to pass through the school gate
- {校門|こうもん}を{出|で}る: to leave through the school gate

WATCH OUT:
- {肛門|こうもん}: anus (same reading, very different meaning — be careful!)
- {顧問|こもん}: adviser (similar but different reading)
